old: A unit of current quietly credits a man who studied the forces flowing through wires.
It's named for a French physicist who died in 1836.
Say his surname, André-Marie ___, and you've nearly said the word.
clues: This scientific unit of measurement honors a French physicist who lived from 1775 to 1836, so his memory travels with every reading taken.
It measures how much electric current flows through a wire, not the electrical push behind it like a volt, nor the power used like a watt.
A typical household circuit breaker trips when the current running through it climbs past about 15 or 20 of these units.
